description: Creates a single, one-off calendar event on the household calendar. Timed events need startDateTime; all-day events need startDate (plus endDate for several days). Set reminders with reminderOffsetMinutes. For a repeating schedule use create_recurring_calendar_event instead.

endDate.description: All-day only: LAST day, inclusive, YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for a single day. The event may cover at most 366 days, between 1900 and 2200.

endDateTime.description: End of a timed event, ISO 8601 UTC. Must not precede startDateTime. For all-day events send endDate instead. An all-day event sent with endDateTime and no startDate stores it as given, and a midnight endDateTime then names the LAST day (inclusive).

isAllDay.description: True for all-day, false for timed.

location.description: Where it happens. $type 'Address' takes line1-3/postalCode/countryCode; 'OnlineLocation' takes url/notes.

line1.description: Address line 1. An Address needs one of line1-3 or postalCode.

line2.description: Address line 2, e.g. flat or suite.

notes.description: Access detail, e.g. parking or passcode.

reminderOffsetMinutes.description: Reminder lead times, in minutes before the event starts. Each value is whole hours, 60-1380 (1-23 hours), or whole days, a multiple of 1440 up to 525600 (365 days); a week is 10080. Up to 5 values. An all-day event counts from 00:00 on its first day, so 300 (5 hours) is 19:00 the evening before. Day and week reminders arrive at 19:00 on the earlier day; hour reminders arrive that many hours before the start, or up to 15 minutes earlier. Every household member is reminded.

items.description: One lead time in minutes: whole hours 60-1380, or a multiple of 1440 for days.

startDate.description: All-day only (preferred for all-day): first day, YYYY-MM-DD. Takes precedence over startDateTime. Stored as startDateTime 00:00Z on this day, with endDateTime 00:00Z on the last day (null for a single day).

startDateTime.description: Start of a timed event, ISO 8601 UTC with a Z suffix. For an all-day event send startDate instead; when startDate is present this is ignored.

timezone.description: IANA zone for the wall-clock times, e.g. 'Europe/London'. Null means UTC. Not stored when an all-day event is sent with startDate.

name: create_calendar_event
